references.text: Phinehas blew the trumpets during the war against the Midianites, as a practical example of blowing trumpets in battle.
At Jericho, the priests blew trumpets as part of God's strategy for victory, demonstrating the use of trumpets in warfare.
Gideon and his men blew trumpets during the fight against the Midianites, and the Lord gave them victory.
The priests blew trumpets during the war against Jeroboam, and Israel cried out to the Lord and was saved.
Jehoshaphat prayed to the Lord for deliverance from the enemy, and God remembered His people and saved them.
The psalm speaks of crying out to God in the day of trouble, and He will rescue – parallel to the promise of being remembered by God.
The psalm mentions blowing the trumpet and that God answered the people in distress – a clear parallel to the promise in Numbers 4.
God looked upon the people's distress and remembered His covenant with them, just as He promises to remember them when they blow the trumpets.
Hosea describes the enemy as an eagle over the house of the Lord – context of hostile attack and distress.
Joel calls for blowing the trumpet in Zion as a warning of the day of the Lord and a call to repentance.
